### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via validateCapabilityReferences (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/view (route, a path literal in paragraphs))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e7d203b17fe6b879b22245edb1a2c0f2d39d9571` — the merge of head `79747fd0ce56da89307fd233e4da4d37620d9e6a` into base `c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e7d203b17fe6b879b22245edb1a2c0f2d39d9571 && git checkout e7d203b17fe6b879b22245edb1a2c0f2d39d9571
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461 79747fd0ce56da89307fd233e4da4d37620d9e6a && git checkout -B drift-repro c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461 && git merge --no-ff 79747fd0ce56da89307fd233e4da4d37620d9e6a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `79747fd0ce56da89307fd233e4da4d37620d9e6a`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #22161 (its body and all 50 comments — slice 1's record `6072212345`, slices 7 and 8's ACCEPTs and landings, the slice 9 claim `6105685119`, the dev report `6106710341` and the ACCEPT `6106726806`, the last three taken as claims), PR #22799 (its body, its 25-file list, and the net diff against `main` at the merge base `e84aeb36ce`: 25 files, +1473 / -182), the check-runs on the head, the sources each rewritten sentence cites, and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` at `origin/main` for what a DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmation must carry — all by `gh api` and `git show`; no checkout, build, test, gate run or ablation.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept set is unchanged in all ten rule files.** Every changed line is a `message` expression, a comment, a message-only helper or constant, or a removed value that fed only the message. No condition, severity, `path`, `hint`, rule id, skip or dedupe moved; the diff holds no `hint:` hunk (hints appear only as context lines). File by file:

- `validate-nav-access.ts` (+4/-4): one `message` literal. The opening `navigation exposes object "…"` is kept, which `examples/app-showcase/test/nav-and-detail-grants.test.ts` (not in the diff) pins. **Right.**
- `validate-nav-object-servability.ts` (+7/-16): the locals `condition` and `answer` go; the base read them only in the message. `apiDisabled` and `offendingKey` stay (`:139`, `:140` at the head) and the new message reads them (`:158`–`:159`). **Right.**
- `validate-nav-target-refs.ts` (+6/-8): one message; `collection`, `noun` and `emptyCollection` are read as before. **Right.**
- `validate-object-field-refs.ts` (+11/-43): the `consequence` member leaves `ListPosition`, `FieldNameSlot` and `INDEX_POSITION`, and the `judge` parameter that carried it. At the base, `judge` read it once, in `message: ${account.message} ${at.consequence}`; now `message: account.message`. The hint `${at.prescription} ${account.detail}`, `resolveName`, and the three call sites' `against`, `name`, `verbatim`, `subject`, `where`, `path` and `prescription` are unchanged. At the head the word `consequence` survives only in a doc comment (`:84`). **Right.**
- `validate-object-references.ts` (+5/-4): one message, `object-reference-unregistered-platform`; `object-reference-unknown` is untouched. **Right.**
- `validate-capability-references.ts` (+5/-3): one message. Its four named sources are the rule's own known set: the built-ins, `stack.capabilities` via `defineCapability` (`:89`–`:90`), `systemPermissions` (`:94`) and `sys_capability` seeds (`:97`). **Right.**
- `validate-action-name-refs.ts` (+35/-22): `atMostThree` (new, module-private, string in, string out); the `consequence` default of `check()` becomes a clause and its two explicit callers (the alert and the header) pass clauses; three messages rewritten. `RELATED_LIST_LOCATIONS` still gates the placement arm (`:412`) and still feeds `RELATED_LIST_PLACEMENTS` in both related-list hints (`:402`, `:428`). **Right.**
- `validate-mapping-target-fields.ts` (+23/-28): `dottedReason` becomes `dottedVerdict` (string in, string out; the `objectName` argument it stopped reading goes, and `where` still carries the object at `:161`); `capitalize`, called only by `dottedReason`, goes; two messages rewritten, one arm reading `dottedVerdict` for a dotted head and the unknown-field sentence plus `suggestName` otherwise, the same branch as at the base. **Right.**
- `validate-view-containers.ts` (+11/-7): two messages. `looksFlat` is unchanged (`!hasContainerSlot` and one of `type`, `columns`, `data`, `filter`, `sort` present, `:149`–`:150`). The flat arm's new sentence is TRUE: `ViewSchema` is a `lazySchema` over a `strictObject` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:4929`), so a flat object's single-view keys are refused, not stripped; `isViewContainerShaped` (`packages/spec/src/ui/assembled-views.zod.ts:196`) returns false for `viewKind` / `config` and for any of `type`, `columns`, `sections`, `data`, `filter`, `sort` at the top level; the ObjectQL registration loop refuses by it with `code = 'INVALID_METADATA'`, `status = 422` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:7703`–`:7715`). The old sentence ("`ViewSchema` strips its keys, so it parses to an EMPTY container") is false for the same reason, as the module header has recorded since #6073. The new test holds both seams (`ViewSchema.safeParse` false and `isViewContainerShaped` false on both single-view shapes; `isViewContainerShaped` true on `{ listViews: {} }`). **Right.**
- `validate-page-visualization-bindings.ts` (+9/-12): one message; `describeSearch` still feeds the hint (`:481`); `leading`, `sourceView` and `predicate.viewBlocks[0]` are read as before. **Right.**

**No export added, removed or renamed.** `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/package.json` and `packages/cli` are not in the diff. All ten ids already have exported constants re-exported from the barrel (`index.ts:685`, `:449`, `:437`, `:515`, `:429`, `:288`, `:522`, `:618`, `:188`, `:550`). **Right.**

**`rule-explanations.ts` is additions only** (+329/-0): ten entries and one shared constant, keyed `nav-object-ungranted`, `nav-object-unservable`, `nav-target-unresolved`, `object-field-ref-unknown`, `object-reference-unregistered-platform`, `capability-reference-unknown`, `action-name-undefined`, `mapping-target-field-unknown`, `view-container-shape` and `page/visualization-without-binding`, each equal to the exported constant's string in its rule file. The 111 earlier entries are untouched. **Right.**

**Moved reasoning, neither lost nor invented**, spot-checked against the base messages and the sources:
- `NAV_INDEPENDENT_CONDITIONS` carries the base unservable message's "cannot be rescued with `requiredPermissions`: they are independent conditions" and the ungranted hint's gating sentence, once, under both ids. Right.
- `object-field-ref-unknown`: every base `consequence` is in the entry — the four `highlightFields` consumers, `redactFields` failing OPEN, the index skipped whole at sync with a `unique` index unenforced, and the four field-level slots (`relatedListColumns`, `lookupColumns`, `lookupFilters[].field`, `dependsOn` on the owner and on the reference). `PICKER_FIELD_TYPES` is `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` (`:338`). Right.
- `nav-target-unresolved`: the three `pageNames` / `reportNames` / `dashboardNames` non-empty gates are `stack.zod.ts:3042`, `:3047`, `:3052`; "if another package provides the target, the warning is expected" is carried. Right.
- `page/visualization-without-binding`: the forced view type and refusal screen, the SILENT drop with the switcher still shown, and the `describeSearch` table are all present; the table is held to `OBJECTUI_DERIVATION_PREDICATES` by the test. Right.
- Facts the entries cite exist at the head: `canServeApiOperation` (`spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts:457`); `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `PLATFORM_OBJECT_PREFIXES = ['sys_', 'cloud_', 'ai_']` (`spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts:162`, `:174`); `unknownImportMappingTargets` (`spec/src/data/import-mapping-target.ts:320`); `validateNavAccess` walks `app.navigation` and `areas[].navigation` (`:110`, `:113`) while the other two nav rules also walk `areas[].items` (`:176`–`:182`, `:158`–`:163`). Right.

**Tests.** The removed lines in the ten test files are old-text message pins (moved to the new verdict or to the explanation), import wraps, and one suite-member pin re-pointed to the unwrapped import (`validatePageVisualizationBindingsUnrecorded`, still the real function). No refusal, rule id, severity, `path`, `where` or hint assertion is removed. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22161-lint-slice-9-one-line.md`: `@objectstack/lint` **patch**, `Clause-②: no` on its own line (line 7), agreeing with the PR body's line 2 and the claim `6105685119`. **Right**, on slice 1's record (`6072212345` ②): RULE_EXPLANATIONS entries are data in an existing export, and no export, subpath, type, severity, hint or accept set moves. Release state at `origin/main`: `.changeset/pre.json` mode `pre`, tag `next`, the fixed group, where stage 1's pending `minor` and slice 7's pending `minor` already set the group's bump, so this level moves no version number.

**Every door the changeset names prints these ids, and no door is missing**, read from the registry at the head:
- `AUTHORING_COMMANDS = ['validate', 'build', 'lint']` (`authoring-rules.ts:161`). `validateCapabilityReferences` (`:1311`–`:1322`) and `validateViewContainers` (`:781`–`:788`) are `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`. `validateReferenceIntegrity` (`:1029`–`:1159`) is `commands: ALL`, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'view', 'object', 'dataset', 'report']`, and `reference-integrity-suite.ts` dispatches `validateObjectFieldRefs` on `['flow', 'object']` (`:351`), `validateObjectReferences` on `['flow', 'dataset']` (`:224`), and `validateActionNameRefs`, `validatePageVisualizationBindings`, `validateMappingTargetFields`, `validateNavAccess`, `validateNavTargetRefs` and `validateNavObjectServability` on the default `['flow']` (`:192`; `:352`, `:386`, `:439`, `:440`, `:447`, `:465`).
- CLI faces, each real: `os validate`; `os build` (`build.ts` extends `Compile`); `os compile`, which `os dev` spawns (`dev.ts:429`, `:932`); `os lint` (`runAuthoringRules('lint', …)`, `lint.ts:681`); `os verify` (`VERIFY_RULE_COMMAND = 'validate'`, `author-time-rules.ts:89`); the scaffold check `os init` runs (`validateScaffold`, `SCAFFOLD_RULE_COMMAND = 'build'`). `os generate` is not named, which is correct (next section). Right.
- Runtime publish gate: an `object` write reaches `object-field-ref-unknown` (an error, so the 422 issue and the refusal log line); a `dataset` write reaches `object-reference-unregistered-platform` (a warning, so the 2xx `advisories` entry and the advisory log line). The eight flow-dispatched members judge no flow-owned site (the object-reference sites are field `reference`, view `object`, action params, dashboard filters, dataset `object` and nav `requiresObject`; the field-name lists are objects'), so a `flow` write prints none of the ten; `capability-reference-unknown` and `view-container-shape` are CLI-only. The dev's probe readings agree with this; the registry reading is the judgment. Right.
- "A tool that matched the old message text should match on `rule` and `path` instead" is stated. Right.

### DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmation (the three pending notes this PR did not add)

`landing-operations.md` at `origin/main` (lines 15–16): a `check-empty-changeset` red of the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class is confirmed by a PASS record at tier on the same head, and that record must name every modified note and judge each rewritten sentence — this section does both. The PR modifies three changesets it did not add, one line each (`git diff --numstat e84aeb36ce..79747fd0ce`: 1/1, 1/1, 1/1), and `Check Changeset` is red for that reason alone.

1. `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-5-one-line.md`, line 17.
   - at the merge base: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` and `os generate` run print the new `message` on the text face, and `os validate --json` and `os build --json` carry it …"
   - at the head: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` runs print the new `message` on the text face, and `os validate --json` and `os build --json` carry it …"
   - The new sentence is TRUE (measurement below). Nothing else changed: the file minus line 17 hashes identically at base and head; lines 1–3 (`"@objectstack/lint": patch`) and line 7 (`Clause-②: no`) are byte-identical; 18 lines before and after.
2. `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-6-one-line.md`, line 19.
   - at the merge base: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` and `os generate` run print the new `message` on the text face, and `os validate --json` and `os build --json` carry it …"
   - at the head: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` runs print the new `message` on the text face, and `os validate --json` and `os build --json` carry it …"
   - TRUE. The file minus line 19 is identical at base and head; front matter `"@objectstack/lint": patch` and line 7 `Clause-②: no` byte-identical; 20 lines before and after.
3. `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-7-one-line.md`, line 20.
   - at the merge base: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` and `os generate` run print the new `message` on the text face for the approval, agent, view-reference and chart ids and for the three `unique/*` ids, …"
   - at the head: "… `os lint`, `os verify`, and the scaffold check `os init` runs print the new `message` on the text face for the approval, agent, view-reference and chart ids and for the three `unique/*` ids, …"
   - TRUE. The file minus line 20 is identical at base and head; front matter `"@objectstack/lint": minor` and line 7 `Clause-②: yes (widening: three rule id constants exported from the barrel)` byte-identical; 21 lines before and after.

**Why the new sentences are true and the old ones false**, measured at the head: `git grep validateScaffold` over `packages/cli/src` finds one caller, `commands/init.ts:1314` (import at `:22`), besides the definition `utils/scaffold-validate.ts:134`. `commands/generate.ts` imports nothing from `@objectstack/lint` (it is absent from the 15 non-test importers under `packages/cli/src`), nothing from `scaffold-validate.js` or `author-time-rules.js`; the utils it imports (`scaffold-wiring.ts`, `stack-collections.ts`, `emitted-source-parses.ts`, `importable-binding.ts`, `project-namespace.ts`, `metadata-file-name.ts`) import no lint entry; it spawns no command; after writing, `runMetadataGeneration` reloads the config through `measureStackReach` and counts the item (`:1836`–`:1842`) without running a rule. The "metadata-generation rubric" is `os lint --eval` (`lint.ts:1240`, `lint/score.ts`), not `os generate`. So `os generate` never printed any rule's message: the base clause named a door that does not exist, and the corrected clause is the only false door claim in the three notes — no other `os generate` mention survives in them (0 in each at the head), and their other door clauses were judged by their own slices' records (`6100276543`, `6101497297`, `6103394547`) against the same registry rows read in ②.

**All three are still PENDING**: present on `origin/main` (`9f5eca52b3`) and byte-equal there to the merge base (`git diff e84aeb36ce origin/main` on the three paths is empty); `.changeset/pre.json` lists zero consumed changesets; there is no `.changeset/pre/` directory; `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` carries no "the scaffold check" sentence. The correction lands before the release that publishes them, which is the class the gate names. The files are not restored and `skip-changeset` is not applied; this PR adds its own changeset. **Confirmed: the three one-clause edits are the measured correction and nothing else.**

- Deviations (12), each answered: (1) the commits carry no card line, the PR body's line 1 does, and the Part-of guard is green. (2) one new test file for a rule that had none; `index.ts` untouched; the declared rider unused — no `packages/cli/test`, `packages/metadata-protocol` or `content/docs` file is in the diff, and the showcase pin's opening is kept. (10) nine gates run twice — process. (11) trailers model-free — no model identifier in the commits, the body or this record. (12) `post-stamped` from the PM checkout — process.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (3): `field-no-consumers` at 341 characters goes to a later slice of this card — agreed. The `looksFlat` fingerprint reads `type`, `columns`, `data`, `filter`, `sort` while `isViewContainerShaped` also refuses `sections` — verified (`validate-view-containers.ts:149`–`:150`, `assembled-views.zod.ts:202`); a slot-less entry carrying only `sections` reaches the empty-container arm, an error with the same wrap-it hint, so no wrong verdict follows — accepted as an Acceptance note. `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` names three capability sources where the rule reads four — a behaviour description, not printed output; the seat may route it with the card's docs follow-ups.
- **One flag the report does not raise, answered here:** every landing since slice 2 names `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project repo` as slice evidence (its corpus walkers read `packages/lint/src`), and the slice 9 report lists no such run. No known corpus pin trips; the shards that run that project are the verdict (below).
- Hints: unchanged in all ten files; the dev's reading that none points at cut text was checked on the diff's hint context lines; the one inverse case (`mapping-target-field-unknown`'s reference arm keeping `transform "lookup"`) is kept. The card's hint call stays open and is not this PR's.
- **Check-runs on the head**, last read before this record: 33 runs — 25 success (Auto Label, Build Core, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate and its 1–3/3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, the three claim / single-writer / Part-of guards, Temporal Conformance, Test Core 5/6 and 6/6, Type Check × 5, TypeScript Type Check, filter), 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), **1 failure: `Check Changeset`**, and **4 still in progress: Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6**. The red is exactly the DELIBERATE CORRECTION reading: every step of its job is success or skipped except step 12, "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR"; its annotations name exactly `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-5-one-line.md`, `-6-` and `-7-` as present on the merge base and not added by this PR; and `pr-automation.yml` runs on `pull_request` only (`types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited]`, no `merge_group`, `push` or other trigger), so the red does not recur in the queue. No other red. The four shards' conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not wait on them, and landing still requires each of them green or an expected skip.

`Check Changeset` is red on `79747fd0ce` by design. It stays red, and this PR enters the queue with it, for these reasons:
- **The check and the cause:**
